stories.title: Nuclear reactors under construction rise to 79 globally on AI demand
stories.summary: The number of nuclear reactors under construction worldwide has risen to 79, the highest level in decades, driven substantially by data center operators seeking carbon-free baseload power for AI workloads. China leads with 27 units under construction, while the US and several European countries have reversed phase-out policies to accommodate technology sector demand.
stories.why_it_matters: Nuclear renaissance driven by data center demand is rewriting energy politics in democracies that had committed to phase-outs. For data center operators, securing nuclear power purchase agreements now provides 20-30 year price certainty but creates stranded asset risk if modular nuclear or fusion technologies mature faster than projected timelines.
stories.title_zh: 受AI需求推动，全球在建nuclear reactors增至79座
stories.summary_zh: 全球在建nuclear reactors数量已升至79座，为数十年来最高水平，这主要受数据中心运营商为AI工作负载寻求carbon-free baseload power的驱动。中国以27座在建机组领先，而美国及多个欧洲国家已逆转淘汰政策以适应科技行业的需求。
stories.content:
LONDON -- The 79 nuclear reactors under construction worldwide represent the most in 40 years, as rising fossil fuel prices and the spread of energy-hungry artificial intelligence accelerate plans for new plants.

stories.title: Labor pressed to reject inner-Melbourne data centre before Vic election
stories.summary: Australian Labor Party members are urging rejection of a proposed inner-Melbourne data center ahead of the Victorian state election, citing community concerns about noise, visual impact, and energy consumption in a densely populated area. The opposition reflects growing local political resistance to data center siting in established urban neighborhoods despite state-level economic development priorities.
stories.why_it_matters: Hyperlocal opposition in Australian capital cities is forcing data center development toward industrial peripheries with weaker grid connections and longer fiber routes. If Victorian Labor sacrifices the project for electoral calculus, other state governments may preemptively tighten planning restrictions, accelerating the shift of Australian digital infrastructure investment to Queensland and Western Australia.
stories.title_zh: 工党被施压在维州选举前拒绝内墨尔本data centre
stories.summary_zh: 澳大利亚工党成员敦促在维多利亚州选举前否决一项拟议的inner-Melbourne数据中心，理由是社区对人口密集区的噪音、视觉影响和能源消耗的担忧。这一反对反映了尽管有州级经济发展优先事项，但在成熟城市社区中数据中心选址面临日益增长的地方政治阻力。
stories.content:
Residents opposing a data centre proposed for the inner-city Melbourne suburb of Spotswood are putting pressure on Labor to reject it ahead of the Victorian election as they protest its development 69 metres from a kindergarten.

Residents are furious the state government has not blocked a $1.47 billion data centre pitched by developer GreenSquare DC, despite Premier Ben Carroll’s new rules requiring 150-metre buffers from homes.

stories.title: DayOne inks MOU with Blue Whale Energy to explore Distributed VPP in Singapore
stories.summary: DayOne Data Centers and Blue Whale Energy have signed an MOU to study a Distributed Virtual Power Plant in Singapore, integrating battery energy storage systems with data center load management. The project aims to provide grid stabilization services while enabling data centers to participate in demand response programs without disrupting critical IT operations.
stories.why_it_matters: Distributed VPP architectures could resolve Singapore's fundamental constraint of limited grid interconnection capacity for new data centers. If DayOne demonstrates that BESS-backed facilities can reliably shed and shift load without SLA breaches, the model may unlock additional power allocations from the Energy Market Authority for similarly equipped developments.
stories.title_zh: DayOne与Blue Whale Energy签署MOU，在新加坡探索分布式VPP
stories.summary_zh: DayOne Data Centers与Blue Whale Energy已签署MOU，研究在新加坡建设Distributed VPP，将battery energy storage systems与数据中心load management整合。该项目旨在提供grid stabilization服务，同时使数据中心能够在不中断关键IT运营的情况下参与demand response项目。
stories.content:
Singapore-headquartered digital infrastructure platform DayOne Data Centers recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Blue Whale Energy, a Singapore-based company specializing in battery energy storage systems (BESS) and Virtual Power Plant (VPP) aggregation services, to study the feasibility of a Distributed VPP in Singapore.

Under the MOU, the parties would explore an intelligent real-time solution to coordinate a distributed BESS network that links battery storage at DayOne’s upcoming SG1 data center with third-party sites, as an innovative way to optimize available grid capacity, especially during periods of peak electricity use.

The proposed Distributed VPP is designed to pool battery storage across multiple sites so that electricity drawn from the grid can be adjusted where it’s needed at key moments. This could have the effect of unlocking new capacity while reducing the need for costly grid upgrades to deal with peak demand, said DayOne’s statement.

The initial work is expected to include a joint front-end engineering design study covering storage configuration, safety, metering and telemetry, controls, operational safeguards, and potential arrangements with participating commercial and industrial facilities.

“Through this collaboration with Blue Whale Energy, we are exploring how a Distributed VPP anchored at a data center could support greater grid flexibility alongside the continued growth of digital infrastructure,” said Jamie Khoo, Chief Executive Officer of DayOne.

“Coordinated energy storage could create value by bringing together an anchor data center and suitable commercial and industrial sites. Through this MOU, we will assess the technical, operational, and commercial arrangements required for a Distributed VPP,” said Gabriel Lim, Founder and CEO of Blue Whale Energy.

stories.title: Google to build US$160 million water facilities in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia
stories.summary: Google will invest US$160 million to construct an off-river storage reservoir and water treatment plant in Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia, capable of delivering 65 million liters of potable water daily. The facility will serve both Google's upcoming Springhill Industrial Park data center campus and surrounding public communities, representing a shared infrastructure model for addressing data center water consumption concerns.
stories.why_it_matters: Google's willingness to fund public water infrastructure signals how water scarcity is becoming a primary constraint on Malaysian data center expansion. This shared-utility approach may become a template for other developments, but it also raises questions about whether local governments can negotiate equitable cost-sharing as foreign hyperscalers compete for limited water resources in drought-prone regions.

stories.title_zh: Google将在马来西亚森美兰州建造1.6亿美元水设施
stories.summary_zh: Google将投资1.6亿美元在马来西亚Negeri Sembilan建设一个off-river storage reservoir和water treatment plant，日供水能力达6500万升。该设施将同时为Google即将在Springhill Industrial Park建设的数据中心园区和周边公共社区服务，代表了应对数据中心water consumption问题的shared infrastructure模式。
stories.content:
Global technology firm Google plans to build an off-river storage reservoir and water treatment plant that can deliver 65 million liters of potable water daily for both its upcoming data center campus in Springhill Industrial Park, Port Dickson, and for the public use. To be built at a cost of US$160 million, the shared infrastructure will be owned by Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan (Incorporated), or MBINS, a state statutory body that manages state assets, once completed.

Google has in coordination with the state government of Negeri Sembilan and Syarikat Air Negeri Sembilan Sdn Bhd (SAINS), appointed local infrastructure giant Gamuda Berhad as contractor, according to a statement by Google today.

Located along the Linggi River, the reservoir is designed to capture excess river flow and rainfall which is then channeled to the treatment plant to be purified for domestic and commercial use.

In terms of power consumption, Google will pay 100 per cent of the power its data center campus uses and the direct infrastructure costs required to connect it to the grid, a multi-decade commitment that spans the construction phase and operational lifecycle of its campus.

Dato’ Haji Najmuddin Sharif bin Sarimon, Chief Executive Officer, Invest Negeri Sembilan, said: “Google’s planned data center campus demonstrates how private investment and public interests can be aligned from the outset to deliver sustainable, long-term benefits for the state and its people.”

Drew Byrnes, Director and Head of Global Infrastructure and Energy, Asia Pacific, Google, said: “Google’s decision to fund shared water infrastructure in Negeri Sembilan reflects our global ambition to replenish 120 per cent of the freshwater volume we consume, even as our water risk assessment showed that local water sources were not at high risk of scarcity or depletion. This underscores our responsibility to grow our presence sustainably—pairing advanced digital infrastructure development with water replenishment projects, power infrastructure enhancements, and programs designed to upskill local talent for new career opportunities.”

“Building on our delivery of Google’s soon-to-be-operational data center campus in Elmina Business Park, we’re proud to deepen and extend our partnership into Negeri Sembilan. The ability to simultaneously develop both the upcoming off-river storage reservoir and water treatment plant along the Linggi River and the Google data center campus in Springhill Industrial Park reflects our integrated, top-to-toe model,” said Justin Chin, Managing Director, Gamuda Engineering.

“As Malaysia’s homegrown regional clean energy leader, Solarvest is proud to support Google’s renewable energy strategy through a corporate green power agreement. Our 29.99-megawatt alternating current (MWac) Corporate Green Power Programme (CGPP) solar farm, developed in partnership with Shizen Energy and HSS Engineering, is located in Gurun, Kedah, where favorable solar irradiance supports efficient power generation. This project will contribute additional renewable energy to Malaysia while supporting Google’s data center operations,” said Dato’ Davis Chong, Executive Director and Group Chief Executive Officer, Solarvest Holdings Berhad.

stories.title: Brookfield taps KB Kookmin Bank to lead Korea's first GPU loan at US$8 bil
stories.summary: Brookfield has appointed KB Kookmin Bank as lead arranger for an US$8 billion syndicated loan, South Korea's largest ever, to finance GPU purchases for Naver's AI infrastructure expansion. The facility represents the first major GPU-specific debt financing in the Korean market and leverages Brookfield's global capital-raising capabilities with domestic banking relationships.
stories.why_it_matters: GPU-backed financing structures are crossing into mainstream corporate banking, potentially lowering the cost of AI infrastructure deployment for Korean tech champions. If this template replicates across Samsung and SK, Korean banks could rapidly accumulate concentrated exposure to semiconductor collateral values, creating systemic risk if AI demand cycles reverse.

stories.title_zh: Brookfield 委托 KB Kookmin Bank 牵头韩国首笔 80 亿美元 GPU 贷款
stories.summary_zh: Brookfield已任命KB Kookmin Bank作为一笔80亿美元syndicated loan的lead arranger，这是韩国有史以来最大的此类贷款，用于为Naver的AI基础设施扩张融资购买GPU。该facility代表了韩国市场首个主要的GPU-specific债务融资，利用了Brookfield的全球资本募集能力与本土银行业关系。
stories.content:
The proceeds from the financing will be used to procure AI computing infrastructure, including graphic processing units (GPU), KB said in a statement Sunday. The 10.7 trillion won (US$8 billion) loan is part of a larger package worth 12.6 trillion won, according to the bank.

The deal marks South Korea’s first sizable GPU financing and the AI chips will be leased to Naver Cloud on a long-term basis, according to the bank. Banks and private credit funds in Asia are expanding AI financing to cover not just the construction of data centres but also the hardware that powers them, such as chips.

A special purpose company established by Brookfield will procure the AI infrastructure. Other major Korean financial institutions are also participating in the deal, according to KB.

stories.title: UBS finds itself in the path of NextDC's share price bloodbath
stories.summary: Swiss banking giant UBS has been drawn into the sharp decline in NextDC's share price as the Australian data center operator faces investor concerns over capital intensity, competitive positioning, and execution risk on its expansion program. The stock volatility has complicated UBS's advisory and financing relationships with the company.
stories.why_it_matters: NextDC's valuation compression signals broader market skepticism about Australian data center economics as hyperscale customers increasingly prefer ASEAN markets for new capacity. For UBS and other investment banks, the volatility raises due diligence standards for data center IPOs and refinancings across APAC, potentially tightening credit availability for speculative developments.
stories.summary_zh: 瑞士银行业巨头UBS已被卷入NextDC股价的急剧下跌，因为这家澳大利亚数据中心运营商面临投资者对资本密集度、竞争地位和扩张计划执行风险的担忧。股价波动使UBS与该公司的advisory和financing关系复杂化。
stories.content:
The bloodbath at ASX-listed data centre giant NextDC – which is facing questions about its financial health after a significant delay at a critical Melbourne asset – appears to have spread to a new casualty: UBS.

That pain dated back to September 9, when the Swiss investment banking giant was the sole arranger, lead manager and book runner on a $1.1 billion issue of convertible notes. NextDC subsequently revealed the conversion price was $16.695, or a 32 per cent premium to where shares were trading.

stories.title: Singapore's STTGDC seeks US$2.4 billion data center loan: Report
stories.summary: STT GDC is negotiating a S$3.1 billion syndicated loan with Standard Chartered, UOB, OCBC, and DBS to finance its data center asset portfolio. The facility represents one of the largest debt raises in Southeast Asia's digital infrastructure sector this year.
stories.why_it_matters: Singapore's banking consortium is signaling strong institutional confidence in data center cash flows despite global interest rate volatility. For STT GDC, securing this scale of debt at competitive pricing will determine whether it can maintain development velocity against aggressive competitors like GDS and Equinix expanding in the same constrained market.

stories.title_zh: 新加坡STTGDC寻求24亿美元数据中心贷款：报道
stories.summary_zh: STT GDC正在与Standard Chartered、UOB、OCBC和DBS洽谈一笔31亿新元的syndicated loan，用于为其数据中心资产组合融资。该facility代表了今年东南亚数字基础设施领域最大的债务融资之一。
stories.content:
Singapore-based data center platform STT GDC Pte Ltd (STTGDC) is in discussions with banks for a S$3.1 billion (US$2.4 billion) syndicated loan which will be used to finance its assets, according to Bloomberg today citing people familiar with the matter. The banks involved are Standard Chartered plc, United Overseas Bank Ltd, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp and DBS Bank Ltd, acting variously as global coordinators, mandated lead arrangers and bookrunners.

The three-year loan comes with an option to extend for up to two years and has an interest margin of 165 basis points over the benchmark Singapore Overnight Rate Average.

In September, KKR & Co and Singapore Telecommunications Ltd together with other firms, completed their acquisition of STTGDC for S$6.6 billion. Earlier, DBS, OCBC and UOB participated in a S$5 billion sustainability-linked loan for the purchase.

None of the participating banks agreed to comment nor respond to a request for comment.

The proposed loan came amidst a debt binge among data center players worldwide which is seeing signs of a slowdown judging by last Friday’s Nasdaq tech stocks plunge. Since 2025, AI loans have exceeded US$ 650 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The investment is expected to reach US$3 trillion over the next five years, according to Moody’s Ratings.

STTGDC is one of the largest data center operators in Asia with footprint across 12 countries including India, South Korea, Japan and Malaysia, UK, Germany and Italy.

stories.title: Japan data center power demand to triple by 2034, driving nuclear, geothermal comeback
stories.summary: Japan's data center electricity consumption is forecast to reach 57-66 TWh by 2034, up from 19 TWh in 2024, representing 60% of the country's total power demand growth. stories.why_it_matters: Japan's energy policy is being fundamentally reshaped as data center demand forces a reconsideration of nuclear and geothermal power. Utilities and developers who can secure baseload clean energy will gain competitive advantage in site selection, while traditional renewable-dependent operators may face stranded asset risk if they cannot match the 24/7 reliability requirements of hyperscale customers.

stories.title: Trump says US looking 'closely' at report Nvidia CEO target of Chinese spy plot
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump voiced on Saturday his support for the "brilliant" head of US chip giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang after a report he was targeted by a Chinese spy plot.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: 特朗普称美国正"密切关注"有关 Nvidia CEO 黄仁勋成为中国间谍目标目标的报道
stories.content:
WASHINGTON (Nov 1): US President Donald Trump voiced on Saturday his support for the "brilliant" head of US chip giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang after a report he was targeted by a Chinese spy plot.

Trump said the US is looking "very closely" at the issue.

*The New York Times* reported last Thursday that US intelligence officials concluded that a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company, who had interacted with Huang, had been funnelling information to Beijing.

China has dismissed the report as "groundless speculation".

"I have a lot of respect for Jensen. I didn't know about the specific thing, but I hope he's going to be OK. He's a great, brilliant person, and we want to protect our brilliant people," Trump told reporters at his Florida residence.

"We're going to check it out very closely," the president added.

Asked if he would retain Huang as an adviser, Trump said: "I would like to say yes. I mean, unless we find out something to the contrary, I have always found Jensen Huang to be very above board."

"But you know, you are dealing in a very complex issue," Trump added.

Huang has advised Trump on artificial intelligence policy and was among tech chief executive officers who joined the US leader on his visit to Beijing to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in May.

The Taiwan-born businessman has advocated for the use of his company's chips in China, where Beijing has been accelerating development of its own semiconductors.

stories.title: Powering data centers in Japan
stories.summary: Japan's data center sector is projected to consume electricity equivalent to 15-18 million households by 2034, tripling from current levels and accounting for 60% of national power demand growth. This transformation is reviving investment in nuclear and geothermal generation that had fallen out of favor following the 2011 Fukushima disaster.
stories.why_it_matters: The reversal of Japan's post-Fukushima energy orthodoxy creates regulatory and permitting opportunities for developers willing to co-locate with nuclear or geothermal facilities. Regional utilities in Hokkaido and Kyushu with geothermal resources now hold unexpected leverage in data center negotiations, potentially shifting investment away from the Tokyo-Osaka corridor that has dominated deployment.
stories.summary_zh: 日本数据中心行业预计到2034年将消耗相当于1500-1800万户家庭的电力，较当前水平增长三倍，占全国电力需求增长的60%。这一转变正在重振nuclear和geothermal发电的投资，这些能源在2011年福岛核事故后已失宠。
stories.content:
*Nuclear and geothermal are making a comeback on the back of strong data center demand. Jan Yong examines the unfolding trend.* 

Japan’s data centers will consume as much electricity as 15 million to 18 million households by 2034, driving 60 per cent of the country’s total power demand growth. This will triple electricity consumption from 19 TWh (Terawatt hours) in 2024 to 57 TWh to 66 TWh by 2034, according to Wood Mackenzie’s report ‘Japan’s data centre gold rush: the battle to power a data-driven future’.

“Peak demand from data centres is expected to reach 6.6 GW (gigawatt) to 7.7 GW in 2034, hitting 4 per cent of Japan’s total peak load and representing a threefold increase from 2024 levels,” the report states.

However, there is a critical mismatch between demand growth and supply development timelines. A typical combined-cycle gas turbine project typically takes seven to 10 years to complete compared to hyperscalers deployment schedules of under five years.

“This explains why infrastructure bottlenecks are pushing major data centre and chip foundry projects to 2029,” says Naomi Oshita, research associate, Asia Pacific power & renewables at Wood Mackenzie.

Data centers are expected to account for 7 per cent of the power load in the Tokyo and Kansai regions by 2030. Fortunately, the gradual rollout of these facilities suggests that immediate power shortages are unlikely, as reserve margins remain above 15 per cent.

According to Wood Mackenzie, coal and gas installations will dominate these regions, representing over 40 per cent of capacity by 2034. This creates challenges for hyperscalers’ carbon neutral commitments. At the same time, Japan’s renewable energy transition adds complexity to meeting data centre power requirements.

“The decarbonisation challenge is particularly acute given the scale of data centre demand growth,” says Oshita. “With renewables (solar and wind) reaching only 17 per cent by 2030, Japan will need to accelerate nuclear restarts and renewable deployment to meet both climate goals and hyperscaler sustainability requirements.”

Nuclear and geothermal are particularly attractive due to their ability to produce a stable power supply. The Japanese government also offers subsidies to build zero-carbon facilities near low-carbon hubs.

Japan plans to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. By then, it is projected that offshore wind power will become the main renewable energy source in Japan supplying 33 per cent of total renewables. The rest are likely to come from nuclear and geothermal.

### Nuclear comeback

Japan closed down most of its nuclear plants after the Fukushima Daiichi disaster in 2011, resulting in a huge drop in nuclear output. The energy shortfall was replaced mostly by fossil fuel like coal and gas.

Four years after the disaster, the first nuclear reactors were restarted underpinned by stricter new regulations. As of early 2026, 15 out of 54 pre-Fukushima reactors were operating supplying a third of its pre-2011 electricity.

Moving forward, the government plans to rebuild and replace aging reactors by the 2040s. Companies are also exploring Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) which are smaller, safer, faster to deploy and can be built right next to energy-heavy sites.

Nuclear energy is imperative because traditional renewables like solar and wind are not sufficient. Foreign hyperscalers like Amazon, Google and Microsoft require stable, constant and large amounts of power to run their huge data centers. As a clean energy with little carbon footprint, nuclear aligns with the hyperscalers’ zero-carbon and net-zero ambitions.

### Geothermal Innovations

Japan is blessed with lots of geothermal energy thanks to its location within the volcanic and tectonic Pacific Ring of Fire. Geothermal is clean energy that can run around the clock.

As of March 2025, the country generated about 618 MW of electricity which the government plans to double to 1,500 MW by 2030.

After the Fukushima incident, in an effort to shift reliance to other renewables, the government amended several strict laws on natural parks that had previously restricted geothermal development. It also provided economic incentives to promote geothermal energy utilization, as well as made efforts to raise social acceptance.

As a result, the private sector ramped up exploration of advanced technologies to unlock the nation’s deep geothermal potential sparking a wave of innovation in the sector.

Legacy geothermal plants use underground steam to spin turbines to create electricity, a slow and expensive process made worse by locals’ concerns over the effects of the equipment and drilling on the spring water.

Hence, some developers like Baseload Power Japan are utilizing next-generation drilling including deep underground imaging and millimeter-wave drilling adapted from nuclear fusion research.

Other advanced geothermal systems include closed-loop systems and supercritical geothermal technology. Essentially, all these systems target heat sources far below conventional reservoirs to increase efficiency and output, thus expanding the nation’s geothermal potential.

*This article has previously appeared in Issue 12 of cloud and datacenter magazine.*

stories.title: Energy North delays 1GW Australia data centre project
stories.summary: Energy North has postponed its planned 1GW data center development in Australia pending federal government consultation on the project's regulatory and environmental approvals. The delay reflects growing scrutiny of large-scale data center energy consumption as Australia's grid faces reliability challenges and renewable transition pressures.
stories.why_it_matters: Federal intervention in data center approvals marks an escalation beyond state-level planning disputes that have stalled projects in Sydney and Melbourne. If Canberra imposes national security or energy security conditions on 1GW+ facilities, Australia's attractiveness for hyperscale investment could deteriorate relative to ASEAN markets with more streamlined permitting.

stories.title_zh: Energy North推迟澳大利亚1GW数据中心项目
stories.summary_zh: Energy North已推迟其在澳大利亚计划建设的1GW数据中心项目，pending联邦政府就项目的regulatory和environmental approvals进行咨询。这一delay反映了随着澳大利亚电网面临可靠性挑战和renewable transition压力，对大规模数据中心能源消耗的审查日益严格。
stories.content:
Startup Energy North has postponed the target start date for its planned 1 gigawatt (GW) data centre in Australia, Reuters reported. The delay follows a decision by the Northern Territory environment regulator to suspend its deadline for setting environmental parameters.Energy North, which had previously aimed for "first power" by June 28, 2028, informed Reuters it is no longer working to that timeline. The regulator is seeking advice from the federal government on policy expectations for data centres and AI infrastructure developers, with no new timeframe provided.Daniel Hunter, Energy North vice president of project development, stated via email that the June 2028 date was an indicative schedule. He added that the company will confirm new timing once the regulator outlines terms for an environmental impact statement.Project Ares, planned for a cattle ranch 683 km from the nearest city, is designed to be gas and solar-powered. The proposed 191 square kilometre campus includes a gas turbine system, a solar farm, an airstrip, and accommodation for 4,300 construction workers.The Northern Territory's Environment Protection Agency identified ten potential impacts, ranging from straining water systems to disrupting Aboriginal sacred sites. The agency expressed "low level of confidence in the effectiveness of proposed measures to manage potential significant impact."This project is four times larger than a NextDC data centre expansion in Melbourne, which was delayed this month due to energy supply concerns. It is also ten times the size of a Goodman project in Sydney, which was halted due to resident pushback.Another developer, Beetaloo Energy, has proposed a data centre near Darwin, twice the size of Project Ares. It would potentially use up to 400 terajoules of gas per day, based on an estimate of 200 terajoules per gigawatt.

- Construction & Site Development
- 1 min Read

# Energy North delays 1GW Australia data centre project

Energy North has delayed its 1GW "Project Ares" data centre in Australia's Northern Territory. Environmental regulatory hurdles caused the company to scrap its June 2028 target start date.

- Published On Nov 02, 2026 at 11:00 AM IST

## Highlights

- Energy North delayed its 1GW Project Ares data centre in Australia's Northern Territory.
- The Northern Territory environment regulator suspended its deadline to set environmental parameters.
- Energy North scrapped its June 2028 target start date for "first power" due to regulatory issues.
- The regulator is seeking federal government advice on data centre and AI infrastructure policy.

stories.title: South Korea exports extend robust growth on AI-fuelled chip boom
stories.summary: Value of the country’s shipments reaches US$115.3 billion in October
stories.title_zh: South Korea出口因AI驱动的芯片繁荣延续强劲增长
stories.content:
Value of the country’s shipments reaches US$115.3 billion in October

SOUTH Korea’s exports maintained strong growth in October, highlighting the strength of an artificial intelligence-driven boom that has powered the economy, even as a recent sell-off in technology stocks raised questions about the durability of the global AI trade.

Exports adjusted for working-day differences climbed 76.1 per cent from a year earlier, based on the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources’ data released on Sunday (Nov 1).

The value of shipments reached US$115.3 billion, following the previous month’s record US$121.1 billion.

On an unadjusted basis, exports rose 93.7 per cent, and imports climbed 36 per cent, resulting in a trade surplus of US$42.5 billion. That compares with a revised 83.7 per cent export increase in September.

The robust figures come in the wake of a sharp global sell-off in technology stocks, fuelled by disappointing earnings and outlooks from major US companies, including Amazon.com and Intel, that have reignited concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom.

Investors have grown increasingly wary about whether the massive spending on data centres and other AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.

The concerns spilled over into Asian markets on Friday, with a Bloomberg gauge of regional chipmakers dropping as much as 4.8 per cent.

South Korea’s Kospi, widely seen as a barometer of the AI trade, fell 3.5 per cent, with SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics sliding 7 per cent and 3 per cent, respectively.

The market turbulence followed solid earnings announcements and spending plans from South Korea’s biggest chipmakers last week.

SK Hynix reported a sevenfold surge in quarterly profit, while Samsung outlined its intention to boost capital spending by more than 60 per cent this year as demand for advanced chips continues to outstrip supply.

Semiconductors continued to be the main driver of the gains in the country’s trade figures, with chip exports surging 259 per cent from a year earlier to US$56.4 billion.

Shipments of computers rose 497 per cent, while petroleum products and cars gained 80 per cent and 18 per cent, respectively.

Calendar effects may have complicated the comparisons. The Chuseok holidays fell in September this year and October last year, making working day-adjusted figures a useful gauge of underlying trade momentum.

## Rate outlook

The continued strength adds to the case for the Bank of Korea (BOK) to raise interest rates in November, after policymakers stood pat in October to assess the impact of consecutive increases in July and August.

Inflation data due on Tuesday will provide another key input before the BOK’s Nov 26 decision.

The export boom is also putting South Korea on course to exceed US$1 trillion in annual shipments for the first time this year, BOK governor Shin Hyun-song said.

That would make it the fourth economy to reach the milestone after the US, China and Germany, said the trade ministry.

The figures suggest South Korea’s export engine remained strong at the start of the fourth quarter, even as the benefits of the chip boom have yet to spread evenly across the trade-reliant economy.

That divergence complicates the BOK’s task as it weighs strong growth and above-target inflation against weak household demand.

The economy expanded 1 per cent in Q3 from the previous three months, beating economists’ forecasts for a 0.8 per cent gain.

Facility investment jumped 4.1 per cent but private consumption fell 0.2 per cent, underscoring the uneven benefits of the semiconductor boom.

The BOK expects growth this year and next to substantially exceed its August projections of 3.3 per cent and 2.9 per cent, respectively.

It has pointed to continued strength in semiconductor exports and investment, while expecting improving incomes to gradually support a broader consumption recovery.

Shin said that monetary policy will remain restrictive until officials are confident inflation will converge to the bank’s 2 per cent target. The BOK will also release updated growth and inflation forecasts with its November rate decision.

Inflation remains a constraint on policymakers even as household demand struggles.

Consumer prices rose 2.9 per cent in September from a year earlier, and core inflation excluding food and energy registered 2.8 per cent. Both eased from August but remained well above the BOK’s target.

The won’s appreciation has helped curb imported inflation. Continued export strength and large trade surpluses could support further currency gains, although the pace of any appreciation will also depend on capital flows and global market conditions.

The country’s exports to China increased about 134 per cent, while to the US they rose 186 per cent. Shipments to the EU and India climbed 56.4 per cent and 84 per cent, respectively. BLOOMBERG
